::: {#exm-sampling-distribution}
#### Sampling distribution of a sample mean

Suppose student heights are $\Rvar_\iobs \siid \ndist{\mean, \varpar}$
with standard deviation $\sdpar = 10$ cm,
and we sample $n = 25$ students.
The sample mean $\bar X$ is a linear combination of independent Gaussian variables,
so it is also Gaussian,
with mean $\E{\bar X} = \mean$ and variance $\Var{\bar X} = \varpar / n$.
Its sampling distribution is therefore

$$\bar X \sim \ndist{\mean, \varpar / 25},$$

which has standard deviation $\sdpar / \sqrt{25} = 10 / 5 = 2$ cm.
Across repeated samples of 25 students,
about 95% of the sample means land within $2 \times 2 = 4$ cm of the true mean $\mean$.
:::
